poiAFL-desc:
Al-Falah, "prosperity" or "salvation" depending on who is translating, is the bloc of the old Middle East. It joins Türkiye, the Mashriq, the United Emirates of Oman, Al-Hasa, Yemen, the Hejaz and Al-Hilal, and, across the Red Sea, the United Arab Alliance of Egypt, Sudan and Tripolitania. Few regions on Earth hold more of what the world still burns: oil and gas, sulfur and phosphate, chromium and bauxite, and the helium of the Gulf.

It was born from a century of wars. For as long as anyone can remember, Türkiye and Iran fought over the Arabian Peninsula through each other's client governments, until the Arabian War of 2188 ended the contest in a way neither expected, with {{poiAFL003|the Egyptian army sweeping the field}}. Iran turned east to the Central Asian Federation. Türkiye, the bloc's largest economy, and the Gulf emirates turned to each other, and to {{poiAFL001|Cairo}}.

The partnership is uneasy. Cairo has never given up the dream of a united Greater Arabian state, and Ankara and the emirates would rather Al-Falah stayed a bloc of equals. Whether the new prosperity can survive the old ambitions is the question the whole region is waiting to see answered.
poiAFL001-desc: Egypt calls Cairo the Capital of Africa. When the Great Flood struck the crowded {{poiAFL002|Nile}} Delta and ruined the old administrative capital, millions migrated south. Thanks to its location, its services and the careful planning of the 21st century, New Cairo now stands above every other African city in population and industrial output, home to marvels such as the new Pyramids and the Grand Mosque.
poiAFL002-desc: Centuries of deforestation in the Nile Basin, going back to the 20th century, have made the river ever less stable, and signs of floods once unheard of grow more common every day. The first of what is feared to be a series has already struck Khartoum, killing at least fifty thousand people, destroying over a million homes and sending countless refugees on an exodus towards safer ground.
poiAFL003-desc:
Egypt's armies are poor, hungry and enormous, and they have learned to fight with their numbers. In wars with the Maghreb, Ethiopia and the East African Federation they mastered the human wave, and in the Arabian War of 2188 they used it to humiliate the armies of both Iran and Türkiye.

Egypt does not control the Mashriq or the Gulf, but the dream of a united Greater Arabian state lives on in the minds of people across these lands, in the sons and daughters of the lands Cairo rules and in those beyond its borders who are ready to die to make the old dream real. Inside Al-Falah, that dream makes Egypt both the bloc's sword and its greatest worry.
